name: GS10789-GS10790 RVPA-108: Efficient and Clean Cooking for households in Malawi
description: This VPA deploys efficient improved cookstoves (ICS), reducing woody biomass consumption for primarily rural households in the Republic of Malawi. The scenario existing prior to the implementation of the project is the use of very inefficient traditional cookstoves or 3- stone fires, consuming a lot of non-renewable charcoal and firewood. The high biomass consumption has negative impacts on the environment leading to deforestation and land degradation, Greenhouse Gas Emissions (GHG) emissions, loss of soil fertility and soils’ reduced ability of water retention. Further, indoor air pollution through health-damaging pollutants while combusting firewood and charcoal result in diseases like e.g. pneumonia, stroke, ischemic heart diseases, chronic obstructive pulmonary diseases and lung cancer.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Community Water Supply through Gravity Driven Membrane Filtration (GDM) Kiosks in Uganda
description:
This small-scale voluntary project “Community Water Supply through Gravity Driven Membrane Filtration (GDM) kiosks in Uganda” is developed by myclimate Foundation and implemented with Get Water Uganda in rural communities in Busia, Namayingo and Mayuge Districts, eastern Uganda. It will install and operate 30 decentralised GDM water kiosks, complemented by solar-powered pumping, chlorination, routine water quality control and a cashless water ATM system, to provide households with reliable access to safe drinking water.
The project aims to replace the common practice of boiling drinking water, which relies on non-renewable biomass and other fuels. By making treated, safe drinking water available at community kiosks, the project reduces the need for boiling and, consequently, greenhouse gas emissions.
In addition to climate mitigation, the project follows a holistic community-services approach. It is expected to improve access to safe drinking water for approximately 20,000 households, support WASH awareness activities, create local employment for kiosk operation and maintenance, and provide training for local technicians and water committees. The project also aims to strengthen women’s participation through water committees. Additionally, it seeks to promote women’s economic empowerment by forming and training village savings and loans groups.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: GS23737- VPA 1- Promoting Regenerative Agricultural Practices for Restoration of Farmlands, Carbon Sequestration and Enhanced Smallholder Livelihood in Maharashtra
description:
The Voluntary Project Activity (VPA) in Maharashtra aims to accelerate the adoption of regenerative agricultural practices that improve soil health, increase soil organic carbon sequestration, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and strengthen the climate resilience of participating farming communities.

Implemented under the Gold Standard Programme of Activities (PoA), the VPA will enable eligible farmers in Maharashtra to adopt sustainable land-management practices and access international voluntary carbon markets. Verified emission reductions and carbon removals generated through these practices will create an additional source of financial benefit for participating farmers.

The Maharashtra VPA is the first activity proposed under the PoA. It will be implemented within the state in accordance with Gold Standard requirements, including the applicable methodology, eligibility criteria, monitoring, reporting and verification procedures. Additional VPAs may subsequently be developed under the same PoA in other Indian states and union territories, subject to the relevant Gold Standard requirements.
Farmers voluntarily enrol in the programme and commit to adopting approved regenerative agricultural practices. Soil carbon levels are measured through periodic soil sampling and laboratory analysis, while project performance is monitored through a comprehensive Measurement, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) system.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
poa_project_name: Promoting Regenerative Agricultural Practices for Restoration of Farmlands, Carbon Sequestration and Enhanced Smallholder Livelihood in India

name: Promoting Regenerative Agricultural Practices for Restoration of Farmlands, Carbon Sequestration and Enhanced Smallholder Livelihood in India
description:
Prithu is a climate-focused organization dedicated to advancing regenerative agriculture and nature-based carbon removal solutions. The company works with farmers, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Self-Help Groups (SHGs), and local institutions to implement sustainable land management practices that improve soil health while contributing to climate mitigation.
Prithu’s approach combines scientific soil monitoring, community engagement, digital measurement systems, and internationally recognized carbon methodologies to ensure environmental integrity and transparent benefit sharing.
The programme is being developed under the Gold Standard Programme of Activities (PoA) framework, allowing multiple project activities across India to be coordinated under a single programme while maintaining rigorous monitoring, reporting, and verification requirements.
Launched as a long-term climate and agricultural sustainability initiative, the Prithu Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) Programme aims to support smallholder farmers in adopting regenerative agricultural practices, improving soil health, enhancing farm resilience, and generating additional income through high-quality carbon credits. The programme connects farmers to international carbon markets through scientifically robust, measurable, verifiable, and scalable soil carbon sequestration activities.

name: Data-verified Smart Induction Stove Project in Rwanda
description:
The Data-Verified Smart Induction Stove Project in Rwanda is a large-scale clean cooking project that promotes the adoption of modern electric cooking technologies by replacing traditional charcoal and firewood stoves with IoT-enabled smart induction stoves. The project will distribute up to 100,000 induction stoves to grid-connected households across urban and peri-urban areas of Rwanda, enabling a transition to cleaner, more efficient, and sustainable cooking practices.
The project applies the Gold Standard Metered & Measured Energy Cooking Devices Methodology V2.0 and utilizes ATEC's proprietary digital Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (dMRV) platform to continuously record electricity consumption and stove usage. This real-time monitoring ensures accurate, transparent, and fully auditable quantification of greenhouse gas emission reductions.
By displacing the use of non-renewable biomass fuels, the project reduces greenhouse gas emissions, lowers household cooking costs and improves indoor air quality. It also creates local employment opportunities and supports sustained adoption of clean cooking through user engagement and performance-based incentives.
The project contributes to Rwanda's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) and several Sustainable Development Goals, including Affordable and Clean Energy (SDG 7), Climate Action (SDG 13), Good Health and Well-being (SDG 3), Gender Equality (SDG 5), Decent Work and Economic Growth (SDG 8), and No Poverty (SDG 1).
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: Rossmann Nicaragua - Reforesting diverse native tree species in East Nicaragua
description:
The project proponent is Rossmann Beteiligungs GmbH. The project “Rossmann Nicaragua - Reforesting diverse native tree species in East Nicaragua” is an ambitious private-led environmental project aimed at transforming 936 hectares of degraded slash & burn land in the tropical lowland of East Nicaragua into a thriving, diverse native forest ecosystem. The project activities encompass an afforestation/reforestation activity that mitigates climate change: The establishment of a mainly native tree species reforestation at an area which has been used so far for cattle, applying „slash and burn“ practices for at least the last two decades. The cattle was grazing throughout the majority of the year and the bush was burned down and slashed frequently to enable new grass growth.
The project does not only include the reforestation of 21 mainly native trees but also additional forest islands, 200 ha which were protected from slash & burn and are not eligible as project activities. They serve as biodiversity habitats and bridges for wandering animals seeking new habitats.
 
The local communities in the neighborhoods will be involved in the project as additional jobs and benefits will be created. The project site will be operated by Ritter Sport Nicaragua, who represents an adjacent certified Gold Standard afforestation project.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: GS23711- Mozambique Off Grid Electrification VPA1
description: +SOL, the Mozambique Accelerator for Off-grid Electrification, is a programme supporting the expansion of affordable clean energy access in rural and underserved areas through private-sector deployment of solar green mini-grids, solar home systems and related clean energy solutions, in line with Mozambique’s national electrification priorities. The programme also includes a Climate Asset Aggregator function to integrate carbon finance into the off-grid electrification model, including the development and registration of eligible clean energy activities under the Gold Standard framework. Through this structure, emission reductions generated by supported assets can be quantified, certified and monetised to help strengthen the financial sustainability and scale-up of off-grid electrification in Mozambique.

name: BEEAH RDF Project in Al Sajaa, Sharjah
description:
The BEEAH RDF Carbon Credit Project is located in Al Sajaa Industrial Area, Sharjah, United Arab Emirates. The project converts municipal solid waste residues, commercial and industrial waste, and wood/biomass waste into Refuse Derived Fuel (RDF). In the absence of the project, these waste streams would be disposed in landfill sites, generating methane emissions through anaerobic decomposition.

The project applies Gold Standard approved methodology AMS-III.E Version 17.0 and is expected to generate approximately 6,977 tCO₂e emission reductions annually through methane avoidance and diversion of biodegradable waste from landfill.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: SAG Solar Park
description: The SAG Solar Park project consists of a 25.7 MWp (19.8 MWn-ac) grid-connected photovoltaic power plant located in San Antonio de Guerra, Santo Domingo Province, Dominican Republic. The project will generate approximately 42,726 MWh of renewable electricity annually, supplying clean energy to the national grid (SENI) and reducing around 27,772 tCO₂e per year. By increasing the share of renewable energy in the country’s electricity mix, the project contributes to SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) through the creation of employment opportunities during construction and operation.

name: Production of Char-Briquettes made from Agricultural Residues, Cambodia
description: The project will produce and distribute char-briquettes made from agricultural residues, primarily coconut shells, as a sustainable cooking fuel for households and street food vendors in Cambodia. Agricultural residues are crushed, carbonized in a rotary carbonization furnace, mixed with a binder, and pressed into uniform briquettes under high pressure. The project uses waste heat recovered from the pyrolysis process for drying, improving energy efficiency and ensuring low residual moisture and consistent product quality. The briquettes are intended to replace traditional wood charcoal, thereby reducing greenhouse gas emissions and pressure on forest resources.

name: GS13139 VPA-1 ETG Live Better Improved Cookstove Project in Kenya
description:
This Voluntary Project Activity (VPA) aims to distribute improved cookstoves (ICS) to low-income households in Kilifi County, Kenya. The VPA utilizes climate finance to overcome affordability barriers and promote access to clean and energy-efficient cooking technologies among households that primarily rely on traditional biomass-based cooking practices.

Implemented by ETG Climate Solutions SA, a climate-focused organization working on nature-based and energy transition initiatives, the VPA is expected to distribute more than 50,000 improved cookstoves across Kilifi County. In addition to stove dissemination, the project includes beneficiary sensitization and training, user support, and ongoing monitoring to encourage proper adoption and sustained use of the technology.

The improved cookstoves are designed to replace traditional three-stone fires and other inefficient biomass stoves commonly used in the project area. By improving thermal efficiency and reducing fuelwood consumption, the project will reduce greenhouse gas emissions, alleviate pressure on forest resources, and lower household exposure to indoor air pollutants. The VPA is also expected to enhance cooking safety and generate health, environmental, and socio-economic benefits for participating households.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
poa_project_name: ETG Live Better Improved Cookstove Project in Kenya

sustainable_development_goals.name: Goal 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth

name: ETG Live Better Improved Cookstove Project in Kenya
description:
This Programme of Activities (PoA) aims to facilitate the dissemination of improved cookstoves (ICS) to low-income households across Kenya. The PoA utilizes climate finance as a mechanism to overcome affordability barriers, enhance access to clean cooking technologies, and support the widespread adoption of energy-efficient cookstoves among underserved communities.

The PoA is implemented by ETG Climate Solutions SA under the ETG Live Better Improved Cookstove Project in Kenya. ETG Climate Solutions SA is a climate-focused organization engaged in the development and implementation of nature-based solutions and energy transition initiatives that contribute to sustainable development and greenhouse gas (GHG) emission reductions.

The PoA is expected to distribute more than 250,000 improved cookstoves across Kenya during its implementation period. In addition to stove dissemination, the project includes beneficiary identification, user training and awareness programmes, post-distribution support, and ongoing monitoring activities to ensure proper adoption and sustained use of the improved technologies.

The improved cookstoves are designed to replace traditional cooking technologies, including three-stone fires and other inefficient biomass stoves, which are characterized by high fuel consumption, low combustion efficiency, and significant emissions of greenhouse gases and indoor air pollutants.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
